Title: Jev State Reviews (2026) | Product Hunt
## Jev State. ## Turn AI conversations into tests and runnable code. Build and test conversational workflows with Jev. See why each step happened, save conversations as tests, and catch wrong turns before you ship. Export runnable TypeScript, workflow JSON, and an integration skill for your coding agent. Bring your own key for live runs. # Jev State Reviews. ### The community submitted 1 review to tell us what they like about Jev State, what Jev State can do better, and more. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Jev State. used Jev State to build Dial. #### What's great. described a rough workflow in plain English ("route billing questions to billing help, escalate only when the caller explicitly asks for a human") and it generated actual states and transitions from that, no signup or account needed, everything saved locally in the browser. ran the simulation mode (no API key required) with a test message and it correctly matched the right end state with a confidence score and a transition-probability breakdown, which is more transparency than i expected from a free tool. the fact that regression tests and runnable TypeScript export sit right next to the simulator, instead of behind a separate paid tier, is the part that'd make me actually use this instead of just admiring it. #### What needs improvement. the simulation mode only matches keywords you type yourself (i had to click a suggested "done" chip), so it doesn't tell you much about how the workflow holds up against messy real phrasing until you connect a live model and spend real tokens. some kind of canned messy-input fixture set, even a small one, would let people stress test the wiring before they're on the hook for API usage. #### vs Alternatives. the realistic alternative is just writing a state machine by hand in code, or using a general eval framework like promptfoo and bolting on your own conversation-state tracking. those work but you write all the wiring yourself. this gives you the state diagram and a way to poke at it in plain language before you've written a line of the actual integration.

Jev is TypeSafe AI's System One frontier model: unstructured state in, typed probabilistic decisions out. Instead of generating text, Jev returns Choice, Score, and Noul answers with calibrated probabilities your code can act on. Now available to everyone at console.typesafe.ai with no waitlist. Jev from Typesafe is taking over the tech community like the first launches of ChatGPT, Claude Code, and the drops that made everyone stop and rebuild what they were shipping. Jev is now open to everyone. Jev is TypeSafe AI's System One model for typed decisions, not chat. You send unstructured state and get Choice, Score, and Noul answers with calibrated probabilities your software can act on. Parallel sampling lands those judgments in about 70 to 500ms, roughly 20 to 200x faster and 40 to 400x cheaper than comparable LLM workflows, with output tokens free. I luckily had early access via the Netlify AI Gateway, traded some sleep this weekend, and built an arcade for Typesafe's Jev. Not one but 7) interactive games that show what it can do. Give the console a spin, try a game, and tell the team which decisions you want to automate with Jev 🚀. I've been following this team for a while and it's pretty exciting to see it taking the internet by storm.

Title: Predict-With-Jev: AI | Product Hunt
# Predict-With-Jev. ## AI. JEV Terminal is a crypto research workspace powered by TypeSafe JEV. Explore live Kraken markets, compare assets with AI, inspect forecasts, and track their outcomes over time. Test BUY/HOLD/SELL strategies in an autonomous paper account with clear costs and limits. Connect MetaMask or Rabby to review ETH/USDC swaps on Base and approve every real transaction yourself. Built for traders who want to understand the evidence, test new ideas, and make informed decisions while staying in full control. Launch tags:Crypto•Artificial Intelligence•GitHub. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Predict-With-Jev. I built **Predict-With-Jev** to explore a simple idea: what if trading decisions didn’t require a heavyweight LLM call every time? Jev-Trader uses **TypeSafeAI Jev as a fast decision layer** for market analysis and trading actions like **BUY / HOLD / SELL**. The goal is to experiment with a trading architecture where Jev can quickly evaluate structured market signals, make deterministic decisions, and act as the decision engine behind a larger autonomous trading system. I’m especially interested in:. * making trading decisions faster and cheaper. * combining structured market data with Jev’s decision logic. * experimenting with autonomous trading workflows. * eventually connecting the decision layer to real execution infrastructure with strong safety controls. This is still an experiment, and I’m actively iterating on the architecture. I’d love feedback from traders, agent builders, and anyone experimenting with **Jev / TypeSafeAI**. What would you add to Jev-Trader next? Always excited to see new use cases of Jev. What do your preliminary results say, is Jev performing at the same level as top of the line LLMs? @prajwal\_prakash There is llm called Laya which can be run locally and perform at the same level as jev but I've not integrated it here yet.
